training_data.source_name: Boltz-2 affinity module (Passaro, Corso, Wohlwend et al., "Boltz-2: Towards Accurate and Efficient Binding Affinity Prediction", App. A.2). Continuous affinity head trained on ChEMBL v34 + BindingDB + PubChem 1.8.1 (Table 1: "ChEMBL and BindingDB, optimization values, 1.2M binders (1.45M pre-filter), 2k targets at 90% seq-id, 600k compounds", sampling weight 0.25). Binary head additionally uses PubChem HTS, CeMM Fragments (Offensperger 2024), MIDAS metabolites (Hicks 2023) plus synthetic decoys.
training_data.cutoff_date: NO temporal cutoff is stated for the affinity data. The only date cutoff in the paper is for STRUCTURE training: "We use every PDB structure up to the training date cutoff of 06/01/2023" (validation cutoff 2023-06-01). The affinity corpus is bounded only by the source snapshots: ChEMBL v34, whose release date I retrieved from the EBI FTP README (ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/chembl/ChEMBLdb/releases/chembl_34/README) as "Release: chembl_34, Date: 28/03/2024"; PubChem 1.8.1; BindingDB with no version given. Effective affinity cutoff therefore ~28 March 2024, not 2023-06-01.
training_data.endpoint_types_pooled: YES, explicitly and without offset correction. Verbatim predicate: "Filter to affinity measurements with standard type in {'Ki', 'Kd', 'IC50', 'XC50', 'EC50', 'AC50'}", and "Convert all affinity values to logarithmic scale with 1 uM as the reference unit." All six endpoint types are mapped onto one log10(uM) target with no inter-endpoint offset. PROPORTIONS: NOT RETRIEVED — the paper gives no breakdown by endpoint type anywhere (Table 1 counts binders/decoys/targets/compounds only; Table 8 gives source sampling weights only). I searched the full 55-page PDF for proportion/fraction/breakdown statements; none exists. Note the affinity VALIDATION set was deliberately restricted to Ki only ("We retain only Ki measurements to ensure a higher degree of experimental consistency and lower measurement noise"), i.e. the authors themselves treat pooled IC50 as the noisier signal.
training_data.contains_ache: Almost certainly yes at the target level. Human AChE (UniProt P22303 / CHEMBL220) is a SINGLE PROTEIN target with thousands of confidence-9 biochemical assays in ChEMBL v34; the affinity corpus covers ~2k protein clusters at 90% sequence identity and AChE is among the most heavily assayed enzymes in ChEMBL. I could not enumerate the actual target list (not released), so this is inference from the published predicate, not confirmation.
training_data.evidence: PRIMARY EVIDENCE, all retrieved this session. (1) Boltz-2 PDF extracted in full (55 pp) — App. A.2/A.2.1 gives the complete ChEMBL extraction predicate: confidence_score == 9; target_type == SINGLE PROTEIN; biochemical or functional assays; standard_type in {Ki,Kd,IC50,XC50,EC50,AC50}; exclude unreliable sources; remove PAINS; drop ligands >50 heavy atoms; hit-to-lead extra filters = avg pairwise Tanimoto >= 0.25, >= 10 datapoints per assay, discard assays with low affinity SD; plus an assay-level structural filter retaining only assays whose mean Boltz-2 ipTM over 10 random binders exceeds 0.75. (2) github.com/jwohlwend/boltz tree (188 paths): scripts/process contains only PDB tooling (rcsb.py, mmcif.py, ccd.py, cluster.py, msa.py) — NO ChEMBL/affinity processing script; docs/training.md says "Coming soon updated training information for Boltz-2!" and offers S3 downloads only for RCSB/OpenFold structures and MSAs. The affinity split is NOT released. Only 16 validation assay IDs are published (ChEMBL 1528727, 438257, 1572912, 1705740, 157530, 454476, 2114176, 1527798, 769558 + 7 BindingDB DOIs). (3) I therefore REPLICATED the enumerable part of the predicate against live ChEMBL. The public ChEMBL REST API was confirmed down (HTTP 500 on 7 attempts across two rounds, including /status.json), but the ChEMBL Elasticsearch backend at ebi.ac.uk/chembl/elk/es/ responded and I queried chembl_37 indices directly. Huperzine A = CHEMBL395280; human AChE = CHEMBL220. 32 activity records, all Homo sapiens, all assay_type B, across 31 distinct assays. For each of those 31 assays I pulled confidence_score from chembl_assay and all member activities, then computed avg pairwise Morgan(r=2,2048) Tanimoto and pIC50 SD in RDKit. FIVE assays pass all three enumerable filters (confidence 9 AND >=10 eligible datapoints AND Tanimoto >= 0.25): CHEMBL1065425 (n=15, T=0.549, SD=0.23, HupA IC50 21 nM), CHEMBL4334128 (n=11, T=0.286, SD=1.16, 33 nM), CHEMBL5117328 (n=18, T=0.484, SD=0.48, 5280 nM), CHEMBL859798 (n=31, T=0.345, SD=1.08, 47 nM), CHEMBL874440 (n=22, T=0.335, SD=0.86, 47 nM). Huperzine A itself clears the general filters: 18 heavy atoms (limit 50) and no match in any RDKit PAINS catalog (A/B/C). All five source documents are 2005-2022, i.e. inside ChEMBL v34. (4) Separately, Huperzine A is an Active with Potency values in the NCATS Tox21 AChE qHTS panels (PubChem AIDs 1347395/1347397/1347398/1347399, 7671 compounds, 245 actives = 3.2% hit rate), which satisfies Boltz-2's PubChem HTS binary criteria (>=100 compounds, hit rate <0.1, confirmatory affinity measurement present) — so the BINARY head likely saw this pair as a positive too. (5) The one filter I cannot reproduce is the assay-level ipTM >= 0.75 gate, which requires running Boltz-2's own confidence module over 10 binders per assay.

noise_floor.interlab_pic50_sd: GENERIC FLOOR: sigma_pIC50 = 0.68 log units, MUE = 0.54-0.55, MedUE = 0.43 (Kalliokoski et al. 2013, ChEMBL 14, all pairs of independent IC50 measurements on identical protein-ligand systems; 3,480 systems / 10,895 pairs after removing overlapping-author pairs; sigma from Gaussian fit to Delta-pIC50, divided by sqrt(2) to recover single-measurement sigma; the fitted Delta-pIC50 sigma was 0.80/0.84/0.86 at upper thresholds 1.5/2.0/2.5). Companion pKi figures: sigma_pKi = 0.47 (fitted, <2.5 threshold) vs 0.54 previously reported for ChEMBL v12 heterogeneous pKi data (Kramer et al. 2012); pIC50 spread is "21-26% larger than the standard deviation of the pKi data". CORROBORATION (the study Boltz-2 itself cites): Landrum & Riniker 2024, ChEMBL 32 — minimal curation, 65% of same-compound/same-target pairs differ by >0.3 log and 27% by >1.0 log, Kendall tau 0.51, MAE 0.50; maximal metadata curation improves this to 48% >0.3 log, 13% >1.0 log, tau 0.71, MAE 0.27, at the cost of discarding ~99% of the data. Ki is no better: 69% >0.3 and 32% >1.0 under maximal curation. IN-SITU FLOOR FOR THIS EXACT PAIR (computed by me from the 23 IC50 records with pChEMBL for CHEMBL395280 x CHEMBL220, 253 pairwise comparisons): mean |Delta-pIC50| = 1.12, median 0.96, max 3.99; 85% of pairs differ by >0.3 log, 45% by >1.0 log, 14% by >2.0 log, and 8% by >2.41 log. Implied single-measurement sigma = 0.99 from E|d|; direct SD of the 25 pChEMBL values = 0.93-0.96. So this pair is roughly 1.4x noisier than the generic ChEMBL IC50 floor.
noise_floor.intralab_sd: sigma_pIC50 = 0.22 (rolipram / PDE4D) and sigma_pIC50 = 0.17 (cilostamide / PDE3), measured on in-house reference-standard time series at Novartis (Kalliokoski et al. 2013, Figure 9). No intra-laboratory replicate series exists for Huperzine A x AChE — NOT RETRIEVED for this pair specifically, and none is likely to exist publicly.
noise_floor.source: Kalliokoski T, Kramer C, Vulpetti A, Gedeck P. "Comparability of Mixed IC50 Data - A Statistical Analysis." PLoS ONE 2013;8(4):e61007, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0061007 (full text retrieved via Europe PMC, PMC3628986). Kramer C et al., J Med Chem 2012;55:5165-5173, doi:10.1021/jm300131x (cited within, for the 0.54 pKi figure). Landrum GA, Riniker S. "Combining IC50 or Ki Values from Different Sources Is a Source of Significant Noise." J Chem Inf Model 2024;64(5):1560, doi:10.1021/acs.jcim.4c00049 (full text retrieved via Europe PMC, PMC10934815) — this is the study Boltz-2 cites by name when justifying its own curation. In-situ pair statistics computed by me from ChEMBL 37 via the EBI Elasticsearch backend.
noise_floor.implication: It cuts against BOTH disputants, but harder against Position A. Against Position B: 2.41 log is 3.5x the generic inter-lab sigma of 0.68 and roughly 2.4x this pair's own in-situ sigma of ~0.99 — so "it is all just assay noise" does not survive; a 2.41-log gap is a real gap and cannot be waved away. But the 2.41 figure is an artifact of the denominator, not of the model. The 5.0 nM reference is the 3rd-most-potent of 25 pChEMBL values spanning 5.28 to 9.27 (0.54 nM to 5280 nM, a 3.99-log range). Measured against the ChEMBL median (pIC50 7.33) the error is 1.44 log; against the mean (7.13) it is 1.24 log; against the mean of the five labels the model most plausibly trained on (21, 33, 47, 47, 5280 nM; mean pIC50 7.02) it is 1.12 log. The prediction of 1274 nM (pIC50 5.895) sits INSIDE the published human-AChE range for this compound, between the 600 nM and 1700 nM literature records. And 8% of ChEMBL's own internal pairwise comparisons for this exact pair already exceed 2.41 log — so ChEMBL disagrees with itself by more than the model's alleged error in 1 comparison in 12. The honest error is ~1.1-1.4 log, still ~1.5-2x the noise floor and still a real miss, but it is not 2.41, and the 2.41 number should not be quoted again. One further consequence: because Boltz-2 pools Ki/Kd/IC50/EC50/AC50/XC50 onto one log scale with no offset, while Kalliokoski shows pKi and pIC50 require a 0.35-log offset to be comparable, the affinity head carries a built-in endpoint-mixing bias on top of the 0.68 assay floor.

forensics.settled_by_evidence:
SETTLED — (1) The affinity training source is fully established: ChEMBL v34 (released 28/03/2024), BindingDB, PubChem 1.8.1, with the complete extraction predicate published in Appendix A.2.1. There is NO temporal cutoff on the affinity data; the 2023-06-01 date belongs to PDB structure training only. Endpoint types ARE pooled (Ki/Kd/IC50/XC50/EC50/AC50 onto one log10-uM target, no offset); their proportions are NOT reported anywhere in the paper.

(2) The memorization question is settled far enough to decide the dispute, in Position A's favour on the factual claim and against it on the inference. I replicated the published predicate against live ChEMBL: five assays containing Huperzine A x human AChE (CHEMBL1065425, CHEMBL4334128, CHEMBL5117328, CHEMBL859798, CHEMBL874440) pass every filter I can evaluate — confidence_score 9, SINGLE PROTEIN, biochemical, eligible standard_type, >=10 datapoints, avg pairwise Tanimoto >=0.25, non-trivial pIC50 SD, pre-v34 documents, ligand non-PAINS at 18 heavy atoms. Only the unreproducible ipTM>=0.75 assay gate stands between that and confirmation, and AChE is a deeply-sampled, well-folded target that will clear it. Verdict PROBABLY_IN, not CONFIRMED, solely because Boltz-2 does not release the split. So Position A's premise is right — but its conclusion inverts. The labels the model would have memorized are 21, 33, 47, 47 and 5280 nM (mean pIC50 7.02), NOT 5 nM. Memorization therefore predicts an error of ~1.1 log, not 2.41.

(3) Position B's specific evidentiary claims are REFUTED on two counts. First, the 5.0 nM reference does not have a NULL standard_type: all three ChEMBL records at 5.0 nM (activity_ids 154458 / CHEMBL643374, 6180553 / CHEMBL1771986, 15762380 / CHEMBL3635481) carry standard_type = "IC50", standard_units = "nM", standard_relation = "=", pchembl_value = 8.30. The NULL is an artifact of the project's own retrieval path, not a property of ChEMBL, and that misreading should be corrected in the platform. Second, "it licenses nothing" is too strong: the discrepancy is real, just 1.1-1.4 log rather than 2.41.

(4) The reference IS nonetheless disqualified, but for a better reason than Position B gave. All three 5.0 nM assays fail Boltz-2's own curation predicate — 4, 7 and 4 eligible datapoints respectively, all below the >=10 threshold, and two also fail confidence-9 or Tanimoto. The single value the whole 2.41-log dispute is anchored to is precisely the kind of record Boltz-2's authors deliberately excluded. Worse, CHEMBL1771986 is not a catalytic-inhibition endpoint at all: its assay description is "Inhibition of AChE-induced amyloid beta aggregation", a peripheral-anionic-site readout that is not commensurable with an IC50 for acetylthiocholine hydrolysis.

(5) One configuration finding that neither disputant raised and that the panel should record: this run's iptm was 0.7136, below the 0.75 assay-level structural-confidence threshold Boltz-2 used to admit examples into the affinity corpus. By the authors' own criterion the complex as predicted here is below the quality bar of the training distribution, which is consistent with affinity_probability_binary = 0.4447 on a compound that the binary head most likely saw labelled as an AChE binder via the Tox21 qHTS panels. The single-sequence (empty MSA) misconfiguration is the leading explanation for both numbers, and this is testable: re-run with a real MSA and see whether iptm crosses 0.75 and the affinity value moves toward pIC50 ~7.

OPEN — (a) Confirmation of membership is impossible from outside: the affinity split is not published, no processing script ships in the repo, and the ipTM gate is not reproducible. Anyone claiming CONFIRMED_IN or CONFIRMED_OUT for this or any other pair is overclaiming; only Boltz/MIT can close this, and it would take one email. (b) The relative weight of IC50 vs Ki in the 1.2M-point corpus is unknown, so the size of the endpoint-pooling bias cannot be quantified. (c) Whether the ~1.1-1.4 log residual error reflects genuine affinity-head weakness or the single-sequence misconfiguration is NOT settled by anything here — it is settled by re-running with MSAs, which is the one experiment this panel should actually commission. (d) Generalization from one pair to "this project's chemistry" remains unlicensed regardless of how the leakage question resolves; n=1 supports no prior either way, and both disputants were arguing past that.

experiment_design.decisive_experiment:
TITLE: A potency-matched, training-set-membership-stratified rank-recovery test of the Boltz-2 affinity head on human AChE.

THE CORE MOVE. Position A's claim is not "the number was wrong"; it is "whatever skill this head has is recall, so it will vanish on chemistry the model never saw." That is a statement about a GRADIENT, and a gradient needs two arms. So: build two arms of human-AChE ligands that differ in exactly one thing — whether the compound-target pair was inside Boltz-2's affinity training set — and are matched on everything else that could fake a gradient. Then measure rank skill separately in each arm and difference it.

WHY MEMBERSHIP IS OBSERVABLE, NOT GUESSED. Retrieved from the Boltz-2 paper (boltz2.pdf, App. A.2.1): the affinity head was trained on ChEMBL v34 filtered to confidence_score == 9, target_type == SINGLE PROTEIN, biochemical/functional assays, standard_type in {IC50, Ki, Kd, AC50, EC50, XC50}, PAINS removed, <=50 heavy atoms; ChEMBL+BindingDB contributed 1.2M binder records over 2k targets / 600k compounds (Table 1). AChE is a SINGLE PROTEIN target with abundant confidence-9 assays, so membership is not a prior — it is a lookup. ChEMBL REST is down this session (HTTP 500 on /status.json and /activity.json, plus read timeouts, on 5 attempts across curl and urllib — CONFIRMED DOWN, no numbers substituted), but the bulk dumps are up and I verified both: chembl_34_sqlite.tar.gz, 4,859,330,198 bytes, Last-Modified 2024-04-15 (this is the exact release Boltz-2 names) and chembl_37_sqlite.tar.gz, 5,764,252,857 bytes, 2026-05-29. Downloading both and diffing them turns "probably memorized" into a boolean.

ARMS (both drawn from target CHEMBL220, Homo sapiens):
- S1 SEEN-DENSE. (compound, CHEMBL220) pair present in chembl_34 under Boltz-2's exact filter above, AND the compound carries >= 20 qualifying activity records across all targets in v34. Maximally memorizable.
- S3 UNSEEN. Compound absent from chembl_34 entirely (first appears in v35/36/37), with a qualifying human-AChE potency in chembl_37. Zero possibility of memorization.
- S2 SEEN-SPARSE (secondary arm only, run only if the clock allows). Pair in v34 but compound has 1-2 records total. This separates "was in training" from "was in training a lot".

MATCHING, because unseen chemistry is systematically weaker and narrower and that alone would collapse Spearman. Draw S3 first, then draw S1 to match the S3 measured-pIC50 histogram in 0.5-log bins (1:1, greedy nearest-neighbour within bin), and additionally match on heavy-atom count within +/-6. Both arms therefore have the same dynamic range by construction, which is the precondition for comparing two correlation coefficients at all.

ANALOGUE LEAKAGE, measured not assumed. For every S3 compound compute max ECFP4 (r=2, 2048 bit) Tanimoto to the v34 AChE training compounds (RDKit is installed in .venv). Hard-exclude S3 compounds at Tanimoto >= 0.7 (near-duplicates are effectively memorized). Retain the value as a covariate and pre-bin at <0.4 / 0.4-0.7 for a pre-registered sensitivity analysis. Without this, "unseen" silently includes analogue series and the null arm is contaminated.

REFERENCE PROTOCOL, fixed before any prediction is run. Per compound, aggregate over chembl_37 activities with: target CHEMBL220, organism Homo sapiens, assay confidence_score == 9, standard_type == 'IC50' only (mixing Ki adds Cheng-Prusoff variance the model's own paper says it cannot correct for lack of metadata), standard_relation '=', standard_units nM, pchembl_value present, and assay_description NOT matching the non-catalytic phenotype blocklist (amyloid/aggregation/A-beta/propidium/peripheral anionic). Take the median pIC50; retain the per-compound spread and the record count. Require >= 1 surviving record; flag compounds with only 1. This blocklist is not invented for convenience — this project's own prior audit (reviews/idea_panel.json:817) found that the disputed 5.0 nM record, CHEMBL1771986, is "Inhibition of AChE-induced amyloid beta aggregation," a peripheral-anionic-site phenotype rather than catalytic inhibition, and that huperzine A's 25 CHEMBL220 records span 0.54-5280 nM (3.99 log, median 47 nM, geometric mean ~80 nM).

RECEPTOR, fixed by hash. Retrieved from UniProt this session: P22303 canonical is 614 aa, signal peptide 1-31, chain 32-614, so the mature chain is 583 aa. The dispute brief says 583; this project's own run log (reviews/idea_panel.json:228) records the executed run as "543-residue hAChE (P22303 mature)". Those cannot both be the mature chain. Resolve before launch, freeze one construct, and record its SHA-256 in the manifest — the two camps must not be arguing about different receptors.

EXECUTION. One MSA for AChE, computed once and reused for all ligands (the MSA is a property of the protein chain, so this is a single up-front cost, not a per-ligand one). Boltz-2 v2.2.1 (installed in .venv312), MPS, affinity_binder on the ligand chain, one YAML per complex, fixed seed, run list generated in advance and interleaved S1,S3,S1,S3 in matched pairs so that any truncation stays balanced and potency-matched. Predicted pIC50 = 6 - affinity_pred_value (verified against the disputed run: 0.10516 log10-uM -> 1274.0 nM, reproducing the reported figure exactly).

THREE CHEAP RIDERS that cost almost nothing and close the other two planks of the argument:
1. Configuration contrast. Rerun 12 main-arm compounds with msa: empty. Paired against their MSA results, this measures the single-sequence penalty on THIS target instead of asserting it. Prior expectation that it is small: the disputed single-sequence run still returned complex_plddt 0.9297 and ptm 0.9490.
2. Model-internal noise floor. affinity_pred_value1 and value2 are already emitted per run. On the disputed run they were -0.2593 and +0.4696 — the two ensemble members disagree by 0.729 log10 on the very prediction under dispute. Tabulate this spread across all runs; it is the floor below which no absolute-error claim means anything. Additionally rerun 8 compounds under a second seed for a full replicate estimate.
3. Baselines that must be beaten. Predict-the-set-median; 1-NN ECFP4 over the v34 AChE set (this is the explicit memorization baseline — if Boltz-2 does not beat it in S1, "memorization" is the better model of the head); and MW+cLogP ridge. Reported as paired deltas with BCa CIs bootstrapped over compounds.
experiment_design.why_it_settles_it:
It settles it because the two positions are forced onto opposite sides of one number, and every escape route each side would otherwise take is closed by design rather than by argument.

THE POSITIONS MAKE OPPOSITE PREDICTIONS ON THE PRIMARY. Position A's thesis is that apparent skill is recall. Recall cannot operate on compounds absent from ChEMBL v34, so A predicts rho_S(S3) collapses toward zero while rho_S(S1) holds up: a large positive Delta-rho. Position B's thesis is that the head has genuine, published-level, target-general skill and the huperzine datum is noise. Genuine skill does not care about training-set membership, so B predicts Delta-rho ~ 0 with rho_S(S3) at the published prospective level. There is no outcome on which both are comfortable.

THE CONFOUND THE BRIEF NAMES IS CONVERTED FROM ASSUMPTION INTO MEASUREMENT — TWICE OVER. The brief worries that error correlates with how heavily a compound has been assayed. That worry is exactly the primary estimand here, so it cannot contaminate the result; it IS the result. And it is operationalized on two independent axes: an exact binary (present in the v34 snapshot the model names as its training source) and a continuous count (qualifying records per compound), with the record-count regression pre-registered as the confirmatory secondary. If the binary and the continuous axis disagree, that disagreement is itself reportable and prevents a single arbitrary cutpoint from carrying the verdict.

THE THREE ALTERNATIVE EXPLANATIONS FOR A LOW rho_S(S3) ARE PRE-EMPTED, NOT ARGUED AWAY. (a) Range restriction — killed by potency-matching the arms in 0.5-log bins, so both arms span the same measured dynamic range by construction. (b) Analogue leakage — killed by the Tanimoto <0.7 exclusion plus the pre-binned sensitivity analysis, so "unseen" means chemically unseen and not merely absent by ChEMBL ID. (c) Congeneric-series compression in the new literature — killed by requiring S3 to draw from >= 6 distinct source documents with <= 8 compounds per document.

THE METRIC IS THE ONE THE MODEL WAS ACTUALLY TRAINED TO OPTIMIZE. From the paper: continuous supervision is a Huber loss (delta = 0.5) applied to absolute values AND, "with stronger weight, to the pairwise intra-assay differences," introduced explicitly so that "this difference-based formulation implicitly cancels out assay-specific confounding factors." Judging this head primarily on within-assay rank recovery is judging it on its own objective. Judging it primarily on one absolute error is judging it on the axis its training deliberately down-weights. That is not a rhetorical point — it is measurable in the published numbers, and H4 makes it a testable hypothesis rather than an assertion.

IT CAN DESTROY EITHER SIDE, INCLUDING BOTH AT ONCE. H3 is the outcome neither camp has considered: if rho_S(S1) is itself low, then pairs the model demonstrably trained on are not being reproduced, memorization did not happen, and Position A's inference chain loses its first link — "the model has probably seen this pair" stops licensing "therefore a 2.41-log error is damning," because the premise of effective memorization is false. Conversely H2 can bound rho_S(S3) below 0.20 and strip Position B of the claim that the head generalizes. Both hypotheses are pre-specified with their own falsification conditions, so neither camp can reinterpret the outcome after the fact.

FINALLY, IT RETIRES THE ORIGINAL DATUM ON THE RECORD RATHER THAN BY FIAT. H6 is a zero-cost deterministic check of whether the disputed 5.0 nM record even survives a reference protocol written before looking at it. The previous panel's ruling was procedural; this replaces the procedure with a filter that either passes or fails in public. And the surrounding measurements give that failure a scale: the reference itself has an intra-compound spread of 0.635-1.041 log10 across this project's own AChE corpus (mean range 0.848 over the four multi-record compounds), the model's own two-member ensemble disagreed by 0.729 log10 on this exact prediction, and the published mean absolute error on eight genuinely blinded assays is 1.217 log10 units with a worst case of 2.076. A single 2.41-log observation sitting on top of roughly 1.1 log of combined reference and model noise, at the edge of the model's own published error distribution, is not evidence about anything — and after this study that will be a measured statement rather than a debating position.
experiment_design.sample_size_justification:
EFFECT SIZE, TAKEN FROM RETRIEVED NUMBERS, NOT ASSUMED. All anchors are read out of the Boltz-2 paper this session and converted to the Spearman scale via tau = (2/pi)arcsin(r) and rho_S = (6/pi)arcsin(r/2):
- Table 15, "Hit-to-lead affinity validation set" (held-out ChEMBL/BindingDB assays — the closest analogue to our setting): Kendall tau target-avg = 0.2855 -> rho_S = 0.417. Pearson 0.4246.
- Figure 14, 8 blinded private (Recursion) assays: tau = 0.345, 0.085, 0.146, 0.218, 0.079, 0.099, 0.407, 0.374; mean 0.2191 -> rho_S = 0.324. Mean Pearson 0.373.
- Table 11 (OpenFE/FEP+): Pearson 0.62, Kendall 0.46. Table 14 (CASP16 blind): Pearson 0.65, Kendall 0.45.
The honest prospective band is therefore rho_S in [0.32, 0.42]. I power on the CONSERVATIVE-FOR-DETECTION but realistic pairing rho_S(S1) = 0.42 (memorized arm performs at the best published held-out level; if memorization is real it should do better, so this under-claims the effect) versus rho_S(S3) = 0.00 (Position A's null-skill prediction). Delta-rho = 0.42.

THE CALCULATION, SHOWN.
Variance of the Fisher z-transform of a Spearman coefficient (Fieller, Hartley & Pearson): Var(z_s) = 1.06/(n-3). For two independent arms of equal n, SE(z1 - z2) = sqrt(2 * 1.06 / (n-3)).
z(0.42) = 0.5*ln(1.42/0.58) = 0.4477. z(0.00) = 0. So Delta-z = 0.4477.
Both positions make DIRECTIONAL predictions (A: Delta > 0; B: Delta = 0), so the primary test is one-sided at alpha = 0.05. z_alpha = 1.6449, z_beta(0.80) = 0.8416, sum = 2.4865.
Require Delta-z >= 2.4865 * sqrt(2.12/(n-3)):
  sqrt(2.12/(n-3)) = 0.4477 / 2.4865 = 0.18005
  2.12/(n-3) = 0.032418
  n - 3 = 65.40  ->  n = 68.4  ->  n = 69 per arm, 138 total.
(For contrast, two-sided would demand n = 87 per arm / 174 total; I report both and use one-sided as pre-registered.)

MONTE-CARLO VERIFICATION, BECAUSE THE ANALYTIC FORM IS AN APPROXIMATION ON RANKS. 20,000 replicates per cell, generating rank-correlated pairs and applying the same Fisher-z difference test:
  n = 60: power 0.723 (analytic 0.751); type-I under Delta = 0 (0.42 vs 0.42) = 0.046
  n = 70: power 0.782 (analytic 0.808); type-I = 0.047
  n = 80: power 0.836 (analytic 0.854); type-I = 0.050
Type-I is correctly calibrated; the analytic formula is optimistic by ~0.02-0.03 in power. I therefore inflate the analytic 69 to a PRE-REGISTERED TARGET OF n = 75 PER ARM (150 complexes), whose simulation-corrected power is ~0.81 for Delta-rho = 0.42 vs 0.00.

WHAT n = 75 BUYS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT.
- SE(Delta-z) = sqrt(2.12/72) = 0.1716. Minimum detectable rho_S(S1) at 80% power against a null arm = 0.403. If the true memorization advantage is smaller than that, this study will not find it, and I say so rather than pretending otherwise.
- Power for a partial-memorization alternative (0.42 vs 0.10) is only 0.62, and for (0.42 vs 0.15) only ~0.5. A partial gradient will NOT be resolved overnight; detecting 0.42 vs 0.10 needs 112/arm (224 total, ~11.4 h of Boltz-2 alone) and 0.42 vs 0.15 needs 153/arm. This is the one honest limitation and it is on the record before launch.
- Falsification precision for Position A, computed rather than asserted. With Delta_min set at rho = 0.20 (half the total published skill; below this, most skill survives on unseen chemistry and A's "strong prior" does not hold), z(0.20) = 0.2027. The 90% one-sided upper confidence bound falls below 0.20 only when the observed Delta-z < 0.2027 - 1.2816*0.1716 = -0.0172, i.e. observed Delta-rho <~ -0.017. So A is falsified only by an observed gradient at or below zero. That is a real, reachable condition, and it is deliberately NOT dressed up as "we can exclude any gradient."

POWER FOR THE SECONDARY ONE-SAMPLE TESTS. SE(z) = sqrt(1.06/(n-3)) = 0.1213 at n = 75.
- H2 (rho_S(S3) > 0): power 0.86 if true rho = 0.32, 0.98 if 0.42. Its falsification arm — upper 95% bound below 0.20 — requires an observed rho_S(S3) <= 0.003.
- H3 (rho_S(S1) materially below the published 0.42): upper 95% bound below 0.42 requires observed rho_S(S1) <= 0.243.

DEGRADED-BUDGET TABLE, pre-registered so that a slow night does not become a post-hoc excuse (simulation-corrected power for 0.42 vs 0.00):
  n/arm 55 (110 total): 0.69   MDE rho_hi 0.464
  n/arm 58 (116 total): 0.71   MDE 0.453
  n/arm 65 (130 total): 0.75   MDE 0.430
  n/arm 75 (150 total): 0.81   MDE 0.403
  n/arm 81 (162 total): 0.83   MDE 0.388
FLOOR: 55 per arm. Below that the primary is declared not adjudicated and a second night is scheduled; no p-value is reported from a sub-floor sample.

CONFIG SUB-STUDY (H5), sized on precision rather than power because its job is to BOUND an effect near zero. Paired, 12 compounds, two configurations each. If the within-pair SD of the log-affinity difference is 0.30 (of the order of the 0.729 observed between ensemble members, i.e. deliberately pessimistic), SE = 0.087 and the 95% CI half-width is 0.170 — so a median |delta| at or below 0.080 bounds the true effect under 0.25. At SD = 0.20 the same bound holds up to an observed 0.137. Twelve pairs is the smallest number that keeps this bound reachable; 16 would widen the reachable window to 0.103 at SD = 0.30 and is the fallback if the clock permits.

RESAMPLING. All CIs are BCa bootstrap with 10,000 resamples over COMPOUNDS (never over individual measurements), and the primary Delta-rho p-value is additionally computed by a stratum-label permutation test (10,000 permutations within matched potency bins) as an exact check on the Fisher-z approximation. The permutation p-value governs if the two disagree.
experiment_design.primary_metric:
PRIMARY METRIC (single, fixed in advance): Delta-rho_S = rho_S(S1) - rho_S(S3), the difference in WITHIN-TARGET SPEARMAN RANK CORRELATION between Boltz-2's predicted pIC50 (= 6 - affinity_pred_value, the ensemble value from the affinity JSON) and the curated measured pIC50, computed separately in the SEEN-DENSE and UNSEEN arms of potency-matched human AChE (CHEMBL220) ligands. One-sided test, alpha = 0.05, with a 10,000-resample within-bin permutation p-value as the governing inference and a BCa bootstrap CI over compounds.

WHY WITHIN-TARGET SPEARMAN, ARGUED AGAINST EACH ALTERNATIVE.

1. It is the axis the model was trained on. From the Boltz-2 paper: continuous supervision is a Huber loss (delta = 0.5) on absolute values and, "with stronger weight," on pairwise intra-assay differences, a formulation introduced because "this difference-based formulation implicitly cancels out assay-specific confounding factors." A metric that scores what the objective optimizes is measuring the model; a metric that scores what the objective explicitly cancels is measuring the residue the objective threw away.
2. It is offset-invariant, and the offset is enormous. Table 15: MAE non-centered 1.7001 versus centered 0.8569 — 0.843 log10 of the absolute error is a pure per-assay constant with zero ranking content.
3. It survives the reference noise floor. Absolute error does not: this project's own AChE corpus shows intra-compound reference spreads of 0.635 (physostigmine, n=4), 0.837 (donepezil), 0.880 (tacrine, n=5) and 1.041 (neostigmine) log10, mean range 0.848; and the model's own two ensemble members differed by 0.729 log10 on the disputed prediction. Rank order is far more robust to both than a difference of levels.
4. It is a PER-ARM quantity, so it can be differenced across memorization strata. This is decisive: the primary must be something that can be computed inside each stratum and subtracted. A pooled, whole-set metric cannot express the memorization gradient at all, which is the entire dispute.
5. It has direct published anchors to calibrate against: rho_S ~ 0.42 implied by Table 15's Kendall 0.2855, and rho_S ~ 0.32 implied by the mean Kendall 0.2191 over 8 blinded private assays.
6. It is robust to the 7-log outliers this corpus contains (huprine X at 0.026 nM, pralidoxime at 340,000 nM), which would otherwise dominate any moment-based statistic.

REJECTED — ABSOLUTE ERROR (MAE / RMSE in log10). This is the metric that started the fight, so it is reported as the FIRST SECONDARY, never as primary. WHAT IT WOULD ANSWER: whether the platform may quote a predicted IC50 to a user as a number. That is a legitimate and important question, and H4 addresses it. WHAT IT WOULD NOT ANSWER: whether the head can rank, or whether skill depends on memorization — because its noise floor is of the same magnitude as its signal. Published: mean MAE over 8 blinded assays 1.660 kcal/mol = 1.217 log10, worst 2.832 kcal/mol = 2.076 log10; only 30.7% of Table 15 predictions land within 1 log uncentered. A 2.41-log observation is inside that distribution. Combined with ~0.85 log reference noise and ~0.73 log model-internal noise, absolute error at n=75 cannot adjudicate the memorization question at any usable power. Using it as primary would be choosing the one axis on which both positions can claim victory.

REJECTED — PEARSON ON pIC50. WHAT IT WOULD ANSWER: how well a single linear rescaling of the prediction reproduces potency; useful if you intend to calibrate. WHAT IT WOULD NOT ANSWER: the memorization question cleanly, because Pearson is inflated by the available dynamic range (AChE spans >7 logs here), is not invariant to the offset-and-scale distortion that Table 15 shows dominates the error, and is driven by a handful of extreme compounds. Worse, potency-matching the two arms changes the range in both, and any residual range difference propagates straight into Pearson while leaving Spearman comparatively alone. Reported as a secondary for continuity with the published tables.

REJECTED — EARLY ENRICHMENT (EF at 0.5/1/2%). WHAT IT WOULD ANSWER: screening utility, which is what this platform actually wants from the head, and where Boltz-2's published numbers are strongest (Table 13: EF 18.39 at 0.5%, AP 0.0248, AUROC 0.8122). WHAT IT WOULD NOT ANSWER: anything, at this n. Those figures are computed on MF-PCBA assays downsampled to 50,000 compounds each; at 75 compounds per arm, EF@1% is decided by a single molecule and EF@0.5% does not exist. Estimating enrichment credibly needs a decoy set two orders of magnitude larger, which is roughly 100x the overnight budget. It also discards the potency gradient that is the informative part of a curated AChE set. Deferred to a separate, larger study — and named here so nobody proposes it later as though it had been overlooked.

SECONDARY METRICS, all pre-specified, none able to override the primary: uncentered and centered MAE; Pearson on pIC50; Kendall tau_b (for direct comparability with the published tables); the record-count continuous regression; the between-ensemble-member spread; and the paired deltas against predict-the-median, 1-NN ECFP4, and MW+cLogP ridge baselines.

prespecified_hypotheses.hypothesis: PRIMARY. Memorization gradient: Delta-rho_S = rho_S(SEEN-DENSE, in ChEMBL v34 under Boltz-2's own training filter, >=20 qualifying records) minus rho_S(UNSEEN, absent from v34, max ECFP4 Tanimoto <0.7 to the v34 AChE set), on potency-matched arms, is materially greater than zero. One-sided alpha=0.05; governing p-value from a 10,000-permutation within-bin label shuffle.
prespecified_hypotheses.falsified_if: The 90% one-sided upper confidence bound on Delta-rho_S lies below the pre-set minimum meaningful difference of 0.20 -- which at n=75/arm (SE(Delta-z)=0.1716) requires an observed Delta-rho_S at or below -0.017, i.e. no gradient at all or a reversed one. This is an equivalence-style falsification, not mere failure to reject; a non-significant positive point estimate falsifies nothing and will be reported as indeterminate.
prespecified_hypotheses.confirmed_if: Permutation p < 0.05 one-sided AND the point estimate Delta-rho_S >= 0.20. Both conditions required; significance alone on a trivial gradient does not license Position A's conclusion.

prespecified_hypotheses.hypothesis: SECONDARY-CONFIRMATORY. Generalizing skill: rho_S in the UNSEEN arm is greater than zero, i.e. the affinity head recovers potency rank on human-AChE chemistry it provably never trained on.
prespecified_hypotheses.falsified_if: The upper bound of the 95% BCa bootstrap CI on rho_S(UNSEEN) falls below 0.20 -- at n=75 this requires an observed rho_S(UNSEEN) <= 0.003. Skill on genuinely unseen chemistry would then be bounded beneath any level that could license using the head to rank this project's compounds, and Position B loses its central claim.
prespecified_hypotheses.confirmed_if: The lower bound of the one-sided 95% BCa bootstrap CI on rho_S(UNSEEN) exceeds 0. Power is 0.86 if the true value matches the 0.324 implied by the 8 blinded private assays, 0.98 if it matches the 0.417 implied by Table 15.

prespecified_hypotheses.hypothesis: THE OUTCOME NEITHER SIDE HAS CONSIDERED. Memorization did not in fact occur: rho_S in the SEEN-DENSE arm is itself materially below Boltz-2's published held-out level, meaning the model does not reproduce even the pairs it demonstrably trained on.
prespecified_hypotheses.falsified_if: The 95% CI on rho_S(SEEN-DENSE) contains or exceeds 0.42 (the value implied by Table 15's Kendall tau 0.2855), i.e. the memorizable arm performs at or above published held-out level. prespecified_hypotheses.confirmed_if: The upper bound of the 95% CI on rho_S(SEEN-DENSE) lies below 0.42 -- at n=75 this requires an observed rho_S(SEEN-DENSE) <= 0.243. This outcome dissolves Position A's argument at its root: if the pairs were not effectively memorized, 'the model has probably seen this pair' cannot license 'therefore a 2.41-log error is damning'. It simultaneously denies Position B, since it shows the head underperforming its own published numbers on this target. Pre-specified precisely because it belongs to neither camp and would otherwise be reinterpreted after the fact.

prespecified_hypotheses.hypothesis: SECONDARY. Absolute error is offset-dominated: over all main-arm compounds, MAE(uncentered) - MAE(centered, per-target mean removed) >= 0.5 log10 units. The disputed 5.0 nM reference (ChEMBL record CHEMBL1771986) does not survive the reference protocol written before any prediction was run -- specifically the standard_type == 'IC50' requirement and the non-catalytic-phenotype assay blocklist.

Reported alongside the recomputed discrepancy against the protocol-compliant aggregate (the prior audit puts huperzine A's 25 CHEMBL220 records at 0.54-5280 nM, median 47 nM).

A substantial fraction of predictions in BOTH arms will miss by more than 1 log10 unit -- specifically, fewer than 60% of compounds will fall within 1 log of their curated reference.
prespecified_hypotheses.falsified_if: n/a as an adjudicator -- both positions predict this outcome, so no result on it can distinguish them. Published anchors: Table 15 reports only 30.7% within 1 log uncentered (65.6% centered); the 8 blinded assays average 1.217 log10 MAE.

Any analysis whose headline is 'Boltz-2 was off by more than a log' is predicted identically by both camps and therefore settles nothing; that is precisely the defect in the original huperzine A comparison, and stating it in advance prevents the study from reproducing it.

experiment_design.stopping_rule:
FIXED BEFORE LAUNCH. NO INTERIM LOOK AT ANY OUTCOME QUANTITY.

1. FROZEN ARTEFACTS. Before a single Boltz-2 invocation: the cohort file (compound IDs, arm labels, matched-pair indices, curated reference pIC50s, record counts, Tanimoto values), the run order, the receptor sequence, the analysis script, and this hypothesis list are written to disk and their SHA-256 hashes recorded in the run manifest. Any later change to any of them is a protocol deviation and must be reported as such.

2. WALL-CLOCK STOP, NOT DATA-DEPENDENT. Compute halts at T = 10.0 hours after launch, or when the pre-registered list of 150 main-arm complexes completes, whichever comes first. There is no rule anywhere in this design that lets an observed value extend, shorten, or redirect the run.

3. TRUNCATION IS BALANCED BY CONSTRUCTION. The run list is interleaved as matched S1/S3 pairs. If the deadline truncates the list, both arms lose the same number of compounds and the surviving sample remains potency-matched. Truncation is analysed at whatever n completed, with the achieved n and its simulation-corrected power stated in the headline.

4. NUISANCE-PARAMETER SIZING IS PERMITTED, OUTCOME-DEPENDENT SIZING IS NOT. A 3-complex timing pilot measures the MSA-mode runtime, which has never been measured on this machine. n is then set once, before the main arm starts, as n = min(150, 2 * floor((T - t_elapsed - t_reserve) / (2 * r_measured))). This is an internal pilot on a nuisance parameter (machine speed). It never touches an affinity value, a correlation, or a hypothesis.

5. FLOOR, AND THE DISCIPLINE OF DECLINING TO ANSWER. If fewer than 55 compounds per arm complete, the primary hypothesis is DECLARED NOT ADJUDICATED. No p-value on Delta-rho is computed or reported; the panel reconvenes for a second night. Below the floor the study cannot separate the positions, and reporting an underpowered result would hand each camp a number to quote. Secondary hypotheses H4, H5 and H6 are still reported from whatever completed, since their precision requirements are far lower.

6. ONE ANALYSIS, ONE TIME. The analysis script runs once, on the completed set, after the deadline. No metric other than the pre-registered primary may be promoted to headline status regardless of what the secondaries show. If the permutation p-value and the Fisher-z p-value disagree, the permutation result governs (fixed in advance).

7. FAILED RUNS. Complexes that crash, produce no affinity JSON, or return a non-finite affinity_pred_value are recorded as failures with their reason and are EXCLUDED FROM BOTH ARMS ALONG WITH THEIR MATCHED PARTNER, preserving the matching. The failure count and its arm breakdown are reported. Failures are never silently retried, since a retry loop is an outcome-dependent stopping rule wearing a disguise.

8. NO STOPPING FOR A GOOD RESULT. There is no early-success or early-futility boundary. Both are deliberately omitted: at this sample size, any sequential boundary would be crossed by noise often enough to reopen exactly the argument this study exists to close.

new_positions.discipline: Enzymology / enzyme kinetics — bench acetylcholinesterase inhibition assay methodology (Ellman colorimetric assay, slow-binding inhibitor kinetics, Cheng–Prusoff correction)
new_positions.reasoning:
HUPERZINE A, THE SPECIFIC ENZYMOLOGY (all retrieved this session).

It is a reversible, mixed-competitive inhibitor that binds inside the active-site gorge — Ashani, Grunwald, Kronman, Velan & Shafferman, Mol Pharmacol 1994 (PMID 8145739) put Ki = 26 nM on recombinant HUMAN AChE and localise binding to an aromatic array of Y337/F295/W86, i.e. the catalytic anionic site, not the gorge rim. And yes, it is a textbook slow-binding inhibitor: Lushchekina & Masson, Neuropharmacology 2020 (PMID 32712274) name huperzine as their canonical example, mechanism (a) "slow binding rate constant k_on".

I put numbers on that from ChEMBL doc CHEMBL4813953 (SPR on CM5-immobilised recombinant human AChE, 298.15 K): Kd = 17 nM, koff = 3.082e-3 /s, so kon = koff/Kd = 1.81e5 /M/s — about 550-fold below a 1e8 /M/s diffusion limit. (Note ChEMBL stores that kon as "1.81 /M/s"; the unit is wrong by 1e5. A curation error sitting inside the very database being used as ground truth.) Residence time 1/koff = 5.4 min; dissociation t1/2 = 3.75 min.

WHAT THAT DOES TO A REPORTED IC50 — three independent, quantified axes:

(1) Non-equilibrium read window. For a slow binder, kobs = kon[I] + koff. At [I] ≈ Kd you reach 31% of steady-state occupancy after 1 min, 84% after 5 min, 95% after ~8 min; at [I] = Kd/10 you need ~15 min. An assay with no preincubation and a 1-min read is measuring the on-rate, and reports an apparent IC50 roughly 3x (+0.5 log) too weak. ChEMBL contains exactly this signature for this compound: "pre-incubated for 10 mins" → 12 nM (CHEMBL2072352); "measured for 1 min" → 33 nM (CHEMBL4334128); "after 5 mins" → 4300 nM (CHEMBL4481753); "after 30 mins" → 0.54 nM (CHEMBL3385584). Directionally consistent with slow binding, though not monotone — because every other protocol variable is uncontrolled too. ChEMBL has no structured field for preincubation time. Boltz-2 has no input for it.

(2) Substrate. Competitive ⇒ Cheng–Prusoff: IC50 = Ki(1+[S]/Km). Retrieved Km(recombinant human AChE, acetylthiocholine) = 117 µM. At the [S] people actually use, 0.1–1 mM, that is a factor of 1.85–9.55, i.e. IC50 = 48–248 nM for a Ki of 26 nM. Substrate concentration alone spans 0.71 log, and imposes a +0.27 to +0.98 log systematic offset between an IC50 and a Ki for the same molecule. Boltz-2 pools Ki/Kd/IC50/EC50/AC50/XC50 onto one log scale with no offset. Worse for AChE specifically: acetylthiocholine above ~0.1 mM produces substrate inhibition, so above Km the Michaelis–Menten form underlying Cheng–Prusoff does not strictly hold and the correction cannot be applied cleanly even if you knew [S].

(3) Enzyme source. Ashani et al., BBRC 1992 (PMID 1575745): Ki ≈ 20 nM for fetal-bovine-serum AChE vs 215 nM for Torpedo — 1.03 log, same compound, same "AChE". Recombinant human 26 nM. Add erythrocyte AChE (GPI-anchored H-form in ghosts/lysates, detergent-dependent, and haemoglobin absorbs near the 412 nm TNB read — a known systematic bench bias) and 37 °C vs 25 °C protocols, which move koff and therefore any non-equilibrium IC50.

Bottom line on the enzymology: for THIS compound the reported IC50 is not a property of the compound–target pair. It is a property of the protocol, over at least a 1.5-log range, deterministically.

DOES THIS CHANGE WHO IS RIGHT? Yes, and asymmetrically.

Position B's operational conclusion — retire the datum — is correct, and I found a cleaner disqualifier than B gave. CHEMBL643374 ("In vitro inhibitory activity against Acetylcholinesterase (AChE).") has confidence_score = 8, assay_organism = None, assay_tax_id = None. It fails Boltz-2's own confidence-9 predicate and the proposed experiment's confidence-9 clause before anyone reaches the amyloid question. But B's stated reason is wrong: the field is not NULL, standard_type = "IC50", pchembl 8.30, as the forensics agent already established. B is right for the wrong reason, and "it licenses nothing" is too strong — a real residual survives.

Position A's premise (probable memorisation) is probably right and its inference fails, for a reason stronger than the one the forensics agent gave. A compared a human-AChE prediction against a record that never says its enzyme was human, at unstated [S], with unstated preincubation, on a compound whose Ki varies tenfold across enzyme sources and whose apparent IC50 varies threefold with read window. That is not a target-matched comparison; it is a comparison against an unspecified cholinesterase measured under unspecified conditions. It cannot support a prior about anything.

The honest residual, stratified: predicted pIC50 5.895 vs human-erythrocyte mean 6.893 = +1.00 log; vs all source-stated records 7.037 = +1.14 log; vs pooled median 7.115 = +1.22 log. Real, roughly 2x the generic floor, and not 2.41.
new_positions.what_both_disputants_missed:
FIVE THINGS, THE FIRST THREE OF WHICH I VERIFIED DIRECTLY AGAINST ChEMBL (public REST confirmed still down, HTTP 500; I used the EBI Elasticsearch backend, chembl_37 indices).

1. THE "NOISE FLOOR" FOR THIS PAIR IS AN ANNOTATION ARTIFACT, NOT NOISE — AND IT INVERTS THE FORENSIC CONCLUSION. Stratify the 22 IC50 records for CHEMBL395280 x CHEMBL220 by whether the assay description names the enzyme source:
   • source stated (n=12): SD = 0.514 log, range 1.70
   • source NOT stated (n=9): SD = 1.340 log, range 3.99
   • pooled (what the forensics agent measured): SD = 0.975, range 3.99
The entire 3.99-log spread, and the whole "this pair is ~1.4x noisier than the generic ChEMBL floor / in-situ sigma ~0.99" finding, lives in the unannotated half. Restricted to records that say what enzyme they used, this pair sits at SD 0.51 — BELOW Kalliokoski's generic sigma_pIC50 = 0.68. Huperzine A x AChE is not an unusually noisy pair. It is an unusually poorly annotated one. Every downstream statement built on the 0.99 figure ("8% of ChEMBL's own pairwise comparisons already exceed 2.41 log", "1.4x the generic floor") is measuring missing metadata and calling it irreducible measurement error. Those are not the same thing and they have opposite remedies: noise you average down, missing metadata you filter on.

2. ChEMBL confidence_score = 9 DOES NOT MEAN THE ENZYME WAS IDENTIFIED. I pulled the assay records: CHEMBL5117328 (5280 nM), CHEMBL4481753 (4300 nM) and CHEMBL3385584 (0.54 nM) all have descriptions reading "AChE (unknown origin)" and all carry confidence_score = 9, assay_organism = "Homo sapiens", assay_tax_id = 9606. Those three alone span the full 3.99 log. confidence_score encodes a curator's TARGET-MAPPING confidence, not assay-reporting completeness. Boltz-2's headline quality filter is confidence 9. The proposed decisive experiment's reference protocol is confidence 9. Both filters are structurally blind to the single variable that dominates variance on this target. Corollary that matters for the leakage argument: CHEMBL5117328 — one of the five assays the forensics agent identified as probable training members — is an unknown-origin assay. Part of what the model may have memorised is a 5280 nM label from an assay that does not say what enzyme it measured. Also worth flagging: CHEMBL3385584 says "inhibition of acetylcholine hydrolysis ... by Ellmann's method", which is internally incoherent — Ellman's reagent requires a thiocholine ester. That is the 0.54 nM record anchoring the bottom of the range.

3. A MECHANISM CONFOUND THAT WILL SILENTLY BREAK THE PROPOSED PRIMARY METRIC. The experiment chooses within-target Spearman partly because the per-assay offset cancels. From enzymology that cancellation is MECHANISM-DEPENDENT, not universal:
   • competitive: IC50 = Ki(1+[S]/Km) → +0.27 to +0.98 log at typical [S]
   • noncompetitive: IC50 = Ki → no offset
   • uncompetitive: IC50 = Ki(1+Km/[S]) → offset in the opposite direction
AChE cohorts are precisely this mixture. Catalytic-anionic-site binders (huperzine A, tacrine, donepezil, huprines) are competitive or mixed; peripheral-anionic-site binders (propidium, bis-quaternaries, the amyloid-aggregation chemotypes) are noncompetitive or mixed-type. The S1 arm will be drawn from classic CAS medicinal chemistry; the S3 arm from 2024–2026 literature, which is heavily PAS-directed and multitarget-ligand work. Those arms differ systematically in mechanism, hence in the IC50↔Ki offset, hence in rank. Delta-rho would then be measuring a generational shift in inhibitor mechanism and reporting it as a memorisation gradient. FIX: balance the arms on binding-site class (CAS / PAS / dual-binding) and on rapid- vs slow-binding, alongside potency and heavy-atom count; and extract per-assay whether preincubation is mentioned and what [S] is stated — that text is present in a large minority of descriptions. Restrict the reference tier to source-stated assays. As specified, the experiment inherits exactly the defect that produced the original dispute.

4. A BAYES-ERROR ARGUMENT NEITHER SIDE MADE. Boltz-2 sees a sequence and a SMILES. It cannot see enzyme source, [S], Km, preincubation time, temperature, or detergent. Those variables carry ~0.5 log SD WITHIN the well-annotated stratum of this single compound, and more across a heterogeneous corpus. A model that predicted the conditional expectation of the pooled label perfectly would still show MAE around 0.4–0.5 log on huperzine A and considerably more on badly annotated compounds. Any absolute-error target below that is unreachable in principle. This reaches the same conclusion as the experiment designer — rank over absolute error — but from mechanism rather than from statistics, and it sets a hard floor the statistical argument does not: it tells you what number the head could achieve at best, not merely which metric is less noisy.

5. NOBODY ON THIS PANEL HAS READ THE PRIMARY PAPER BEHIND THE 5.0 nM RECORD. Three agents have now argued about it, one has traced its activity_ids and assay descriptions, and the source document has not been opened. For a slow-binding inhibitor that is the only place the answer lives — preincubation time, [S], enzyme source, and temperature are in the methods section and nowhere else. That is a one-hour retrieval and it should precede any further quotation of any error figure. Arguing about a number whose methods section nobody has read is the actual failure mode here, and it is upstream of both positions.
