new_positions.reasoning:
I built the budget nobody built, and I measured the two largest terms instead of asserting them. Everything below is retrieved or measured this session; ChEMBL REST is still down (curl timeout at 25 s on /status.json, HTTP 000), so all ChEMBL numbers come from the Elasticsearch backend at ebi.ac.uk/chembl/elk/es (chembl_activity index), and I recomputed them myself rather than inheriting the forensic report's figures.

=== WHAT I MEASURED (Type A, this machine, this session) ===
Artefacts: /private/tmp/aff/ (the disputed run) and /private/tmp/claude-501/.../scratchpad/rep/ (my replicates).

(1) REPEATABILITY. Boltz-2's `--seed` default is None — no seeding. The disputed run was therefore a single unseeded draw and its repeatability had never been measured. I reran the identical input (583-aa P22303 mature chain, same SMILES, msa: empty) 6 times total (the original + 5 fresh):
  affinity_pred_value = 0.1052, 0.1924, 0.1194, 0.0250, 0.1798, 0.2055
  mean 0.1379, SD 0.0685 log10, range 0.180.
  u(repeatability) = 0.068 log10. The instrument is far more repeatable than anyone assumed.

(2) ENSEMBLE MODEL-FORM SPLIT — and it is not noise. Across all 6 runs, head 1 averaged −0.181 and head 2 averaged +0.456; |m1−m2| = 0.356 to 0.741, mean 0.637, and the SIGN never flipped. This is a reproducible disagreement between two equally-plausible checkpoints whose mean is what gets reported. Treated as a two-point Type B distribution, u = half the split = 0.319 log10. This term dominates the corrected budget (70% of the variance) and no one in the dispute counted it.

(3) CONFIGURATION (single-sequence vs MSA) — measured, and it goes the OPPOSITE way from Position B's assumption. I ran 3 replicates with a real ColabFold MSA (depth 11,145 in bfd.mgnify30.metaeuk30.smag30.a3m + uniref):
  MSA-mode affinity_pred_value = 1.0216, 0.9697, 0.8544; mean 0.9485, SD 0.0856.
  Configuration effect = +0.811 log10, SE 0.057 (Welch t ≈ 14).
  Predicted pIC50: single-sequence 5.862 → MSA 5.052. Fixing the "misconfiguration" makes the prediction WORSE by 0.81 log, moving predicted IC50 from ~1.4 µM to ~8.9 µM. Position B's misconfiguration plank is not merely unproven; it is refuted with the sign reversed.

(4) BONUS — the panel's own iptm finding is a coin flip. Across the 6 single-sequence replicates iptm ran 0.7136, 0.7394, 0.8280, 0.7915, 0.7544, 0.8410 — 4 of 6 ABOVE Boltz-2's 0.75 training-admission threshold. The forensic report's finding (5) ("this run sits below the training-distribution quality bar") is an artifact of one unseeded draw. By contrast affinity_probability_binary is genuinely stable: 0.422–0.463 single-sequence, 0.344–0.380 with MSA. The low binder probability is real; the low iptm was luck.

=== THE REFERENT (the "5.0 nM truth") ===
Huperzine A (CHEMBL395280) × human AChE (CHEMBL220): 32 activity records, 23 IC50 records with pchembl, spread over 23 DISTINCT documents (so they are genuinely independent, n_eff = 23). Values 5.28–9.27, median 7.33, mean 7.096, SD 0.980.

Two corrections the disputants never applied:

(a) ASSAY TYPE IS NOT NULL. All three 5.0 nM records — CHEMBL643374, CHEMBL1771986, CHEMBL3635481 — carry standard_type = "IC50", standard_relation "=", units nM, pchembl 8.30. Position B's central evidentiary claim is factually false; the NULL is an artifact of this project's retrieval path, not a property of ChEMBL. That bug should be fixed in the platform.

(b) PROVENANCE STRATIFICATION — the finding that matters. Splitting the 23 records on whether the assay description names a human enzyme source:
   explicit human/erythrocyte/RBC:  n=12, mean pIC50 7.036, SD 0.539
   species unspecified/"unknown origin": n=11, mean pIC50 7.162, SD 1.336
   Means are indistinguishable (Δ = +0.126, t = 0.29). VARIANCES are not: F = 6.14 (10,11), p = 0.006; Levene p = 0.010.
   Provenance controls dispersion, not location. And the clean stratum's SD of 0.539 is BELOW Kalliokoski's generic inter-lab σ_pIC50 = 0.68 (verified verbatim from PMC3628986: "σpIC50 = 0.68, MUEpIC50 = 0.55 and MedUEpIC50 = 0.43"; intra-lab σ = 0.22 rolipram/PDE4D, 0.17 cilostamide/PDE3; 10,895 IC50 values, 3,480 systems, 20,356 pairs). So the forensic claim that "this pair is roughly 1.4× noisier than the generic ChEMBL IC50 floor" is itself an artifact of pooling in the unspecified-provenance stratum. Provenance-clean, this pair is QUIETER than the floor.
   Crucially, the 5.0 nM referent lives entirely in the high-variance stratum: the four most potent records in the whole set are "unknown origin" (9.27), "AChE-induced amyloid beta aggregation" (8.30, not a catalytic endpoint at all), "AChE (unknown origin)" (8.30) and an unspecified "In vitro inhibitory activity against AChE" (8.30). Cross-species check: HupA IC50 medians are human 7.33 (n=23), rat 7.09, bovine 7.13, Torpedo 7.94, Electrophorus 5.29 — a 2.6-log species span, so "unknown origin" is not a cosmetic annotation gap.
   Defensible reference value: pIC50 = 7.036 ± 0.156 (SEM, n=12 independent documents) = 92 nM.

=== THE UNCERTAINTY BUDGET ===
Measurand D = pIC50(reference) − pIC50(prediction), log10 units.

BUDGET A — as the panel posed it (single random ChEMBL record, no bias corrections):
  u1 run-to-run repeatability (Type A, n=6)            0.068   ( 0% of variance)
  u2 ensemble model-form split                         0.319   ( 8%)
  u3 endpoint pooling on the model's target axis       0.102   ( 1%)
  u4 single random ChEMBL record as referent           0.980   (74%)
  u5 configuration SS-vs-MSA left undecided (rect.)    0.468   (17%)
  COMBINED u_c = 1.139;  D = 2.406;  z = 2.11;  U(k=2) = 2.28
  → D = 2.41 ± 2.28 (95%). Barely excludes zero. The dispute was fought over a quantity whose expanded uncertainty is 95% of its own value.

  On u3: Boltz-2 pools Ki/Kd/IC50/XC50/EC50/AC50 onto one log10(µM) axis with no offset (paper App. A.2.1, verbatim: "Filter to affinity measurements with standard type in {'Ki','Kd','IC50','XC50','EC50','AC50'}", "Convert all affinity values to logarithmic scale with 1 µM as the reference unit"), while Kalliokoski measured pKi to sit 0.355 log above pIC50 (factor 2.3). Corpus fraction unknown → rectangular on [0, 0.355]: bias +0.177, u = 0.355/√12 = 0.102. NOT RETRIEVED: the endpoint proportions; the paper reports none.
  On IC50→Ki conversion: not applicable, both sides are on the IC50 axis. Worth recording that Boltz-2's own authors say the Cheng–Prusoff correction "is frequently infeasible due to missing metadata (eg. the substrate concentration or Km)" and that their pairwise-difference loss exists precisely to "implicitly cancel out assay-specific confounding factors." The absolute level is the axis the training deliberately does not control.

BUDGET B — bias-corrected (the estimate that should have been reported):
  corrections to D:  referent selection (cherry → provenance-clean mean)  −1.265
                     configuration (single-seq → vendor-intended MSA)     +0.811
                     endpoint pooling                                     +0.177
  D_corr = 2.406 − 1.265 + 0.811 + 0.177 = 2.129
  u1 repeatability                                     0.068   ( 3%)
  u2 ensemble model-form split                         0.319   (70%)
  u3 endpoint-pooling residual                         0.102   ( 7%)
  u4 reference population mean (SEM, 12 documents)     0.156   (17%)
  u5 measured configuration correction (SE)            0.057   ( 2%)
  COMBINED u_c = 0.380;  z = 5.61;  U(k=2) = 0.76
  → D_corr = 2.13 ± 0.76 (95%).

The single most interesting arithmetic fact in this whole dispute: the referent-selection bias (−1.27) is very nearly cancelled by the configuration + pooling bias (+0.99). The 2.41 figure was approximately numerically right for two large, opposite, entirely unrecognised reasons. It is not a measurement; it is a coincidence.

=== THE RULING ===
Question as asked — is 2.41 significantly different from zero given the budget? Two answers, and the distinction is the whole point:

(i) As the panel computed it: NO, not robustly. 2.41 ± 2.28 at k=2. The lower bound is 0.13. One coverage factor's worth of honesty and the finding evaporates. Nothing should ever have been concluded from it.

(ii) Properly corrected: YES on this pair. D_corr = 2.13 ± 0.76 (k=2), z = 5.6. The Boltz-2 affinity head, run as the vendor intends, genuinely under-predicts huperzine A's human-AChE potency by roughly two orders of magnitude, and that is not measurement noise.

But — and this is the part that decides the dispute — a real discrepancy on this pair is NOT evidence about the head. Two further comparisons:

ACCEPTANCE BAND (the instrument's published accuracy). Table 15 of the Boltz-2 paper, held-out ChEMBL/BindingDB hit-to-lead: MAE uncentered 1.7001, centered 0.8569. These are kcal/mol, not log10 — the paper states "Percentage within 1 and 2 kcal/mol" and captions Figure 12 "in kcal/mol"; the forensic brief read them as log units. Converting at the vendor's own factor 1.364: uncentered MAE = 1.246 log10 → σ = 1.562 log10; centered = 0.628 log10 → σ = 0.787; the pure per-assay OFFSET component is sqrt(1.562²−0.787²) = 1.349 log10. The 8 blinded Recursion assays (MAEs 1.062, 2.202, 2.832, 1.706, 1.095, 1.739, 1.603, 1.039 kcal/mol) average 1.217 log10, worst 2.076 log10. Only 62.2% of Table-15 predictions land within 2 kcal/mol (1.47 log10) uncentered — i.e. 37.8% of Boltz-2's own held-out predictions miss by more than 1.47 log.
  D_corr / σ_instrument = 2.13 / 1.562 = 1.36. The corrected error is a 1.4-sigma draw from the instrument's own published error distribution. It is IN SPEC. It is unremarkable.

THE n=1 TEST. Position A's claim is about a population ("this project's chemistry"), not about huperzine A. The standard uncertainty on a mean error estimated from one compound is σ_model/√1 = 1.562 log10, so the generalisation estimate is 2.13 ± 3.12 (k=2) = [−0.99, +5.25]. It contains zero. Position A used pair-level uncertainty (u = 0.38) to license a population-level claim that carries u = 1.56. That is the error, and it is the classic one.

Verdict on each side. Position A: right that a real, significant discrepancy exists on this pair (which B denied); wrong on the number (2.41 is not an estimate of anything), wrong that memorisation makes it damning (the labels the model would have memorised average pIC50 7.02–7.04, not 8.30), and wrong that n=1 licenses a prior — the expanded uncertainty on that prior spans zero. Position B: right that the metric is off-task — the vendor's own documentation says affinity_pred_value "should only be used when comparing different active molecules, not inactives" and belongs in "hit-to-lead and lead-optimization", i.e. quoting it as an absolute IC50 for one compound is off-label use — and right that a single absolute error licenses no generalisation; but wrong that the reference had a NULL standard_type (all three 5.0 nM records are IC50), wrong that the single-sequence run explains the gap (fixing it makes the gap 0.81 log WORSE), and wrong that "it licenses nothing" (2.13 ± 0.76 on this pair is a real, reportable measurement, and the head's ±1.56 log absolute accuracy is a real, reportable specification).

Practical rulings for the platform: (1) stop quoting 2.41; the defensible figure is 2.13 ± 0.76 (k=2) against a provenance-clean reference of 92 nM. (2) Fix the retrieval bug that reports standard_type NULL. (3) Never display affinity_pred_value as an absolute IC50 — its k=2 expanded uncertainty is ±3.1 log10 by the vendor's own held-out data, which is a factor of 1,300. (4) Seed the runs; the default is None. (5) Never quote iptm from a single unseeded run; here it swung 0.71–0.84.

Runtime note for anyone budgeting the proposed follow-up study: my single-sequence runs took 379–446 s wall each on this MPS machine (not 184 s), and MSA-mode runs 455–489 s including MSA generation. The proposed 150-complex overnight plan is roughly 2.4× over its own cost estimate.
new_positions.what_would_change_my_mind:
Six things, in descending order of force.

(1) THE ENSEMBLE TERM. u2 = 0.319 carries 70% of the corrected variance and rests on my treating the two affinity checkpoints as two equally-plausible instruments whose mean is reported. If Boltz/MIT document that head 2 is the calibrated one and head 1 is an auxiliary (or that the ensemble mean is calibrated end-to-end against held-out data), u2 collapses toward zero, u_c falls to ~0.20, and D_corr = 2.13 ± 0.40. That strengthens the pair-level finding and does nothing to the generalisation verdict. Conversely, if the split is target-dependent and larger elsewhere, u2 grows and even the pair-level result softens.

(2) MORE COMPOUNDS. n = 3 is enough. With σ_between-compound ≈ 1.56 log10 and a true mean error of 2.1, three human-AChE compounds would push 2σ/√n below the effect and make the generalisation claim testable. If Boltz-2 shows a mean error near 2 log10 with the same sign across 3–10 potency-matched human-AChE ligands, Position A's conclusion becomes licensed — not by memorisation logic, but by direct measurement — and I move to "A is right." If the mean error over that set is within ±0.8 log of zero and huperzine A is an outlier, I move to "B is right." The panel spent enormous argument on a question that ~20 minutes of the compute I just used would have answered.

(3) A REFERENCE MEASUREMENT WITH STATED CONDITIONS. One Ellman assay on recombinant human AChE with [S], Km, pH, temperature and pre-incubation time recorded, run in duplicate, would replace my 7.036 ± 0.156 with a traceable value and collapse the entire reference side of the budget. If that value lands near 5 nM rather than near 92 nM, the referent-selection correction of −1.265 was wrong, D_corr rises toward 3.4, and Position A's premise (though not its inference) gets much stronger.

(4) THE UNITS OF TABLE 15. My acceptance band σ = 1.562 log10 depends on reading MAE 1.7001 as kcal/mol and dividing by 1.364. I justified that from the paper's own "within 1 and 2 kcal/mol" and the Figure 12 caption "in kcal/mol". If those MAEs are actually log10 units, σ_instrument becomes 2.13 log10, the corrected error drops to 1.0 sigma, and my "in spec" conclusion gets even safer — so this cannot flip the ruling, only its margin. If instead the correct band is the CENTERED σ = 0.787 (arguable, since one could hold the model to rank-plus-offset accuracy), then D_corr/σ = 2.7 and the error becomes genuinely anomalous. That is the single assumption most worth attacking, and I would change my "unremarkable" characterisation if someone argued convincingly that the uncentered band is the wrong reference for a single-compound absolute query.

(5) CONFIGURATION GENERALITY. My +0.811 log MSA penalty is n=3 vs n=6 on one complex. If it reverses on other AChE ligands, the correction is target-and-ligand-specific noise rather than a systematic, u5 must be widened, and Position B's misconfiguration argument comes partly back to life.

(6) MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMATION. If Boltz/MIT release the affinity split and huperzine A × CHEMBL220 is confirmed IN with the labels 21/33/47/47/5280 nM, nothing in my budget changes — the model would then be reproducing neither its training labels (7.02) nor the literature (7.04), which makes it a calibration finding, not a memorisation finding. Confirmed OUT would remove Position A's premise entirely. Either way the budget stands; only the interpretation of the residual moves.

Things that would NOT change my mind: any further argument about whether the pair was memorised, conducted without running more compounds. That question has been settled to the limit of what is knowable from outside and it does not touch the measurement.
new_positions.what_both_disputants_missed:
FOUR THINGS, and the first is the one that should end the argument.

(1) THERE IS NO DEFINED MEASURAND, SO "THE TRUTH IS 5.0 nM" IS NOT A STATEMENT WITH A TRUTH VALUE. In metrology you cannot state an error before you state what quantity you are measuring, under what conditions, traceable to what. An IC50 is not a property of a compound-target pair; it is a property of an ASSAY. For huperzine A this is not pedantry: it is a mixed-competitive, slow-binding inhibitor — retrieved this session — with Ki 20–40 nM and a dissociation half-time of ~35 min, and ChEMBL's own SPR record for the pair (CHEMBL4815507/8) gives koff = 3.082e-3 s^-1, i.e. a residence time of 324 s. Its measured IC50 therefore depends on pre-incubation time and on [S]/Km, and the ChEMBL set shows exactly that fingerprint: the record annotated "pre-incubated for 10 mins" reads 12 nM while zero-preincubation Ellman assays in the same set read 47–260 nM. So "the truth is 5.0 nM" is not a value of a quantity; it is one realisation of a condition-dependent family. Both disputants argued about the size of an error whose measurand was never defined. Position A quoted a number; Position B attacked the number's provenance; neither asked what quantity either side was estimating. Add to this that the model's output is not an IC50 at all — the vendor's docs call it "log10(IC50) derived from an IC50 measured in µM" while the training corpus pools Ki/Kd/IC50/XC50/EC50/AC50 with no offset. The instrument and the reference measure different quantities and always did. That is a traceability failure, not a performance finding.

(2) THEY CONFLATED PRECISION WITH ACCURACY, AND PAIR-LEVEL UNCERTAINTY WITH POPULATION-LEVEL UNCERTAINTY. Nobody ran the instrument twice. Boltz-2's `--seed` defaults to None; every number in this dispute came from one unseeded draw of a stochastic process, and the panel treated it as a reading. When I ran it six times the repeatability turned out excellent (SD 0.068 log10) — so the panel was accidentally safe on precision and grossly unsafe on everything else. The deeper conflation: u(this pair's discrepancy) = 0.38 log10, but u(the head's mean error on this project's chemistry, from n=1) = 1.56 log10. Position A computed the first and asserted the second. The corrected pair-level discrepancy 2.13 ± 0.76 excludes zero; the generalisation interval 2.13 ± 3.12 contains zero. Both statements are true simultaneously and the entire dispute lives in the gap between them. This is the calculation the chair should have demanded.

(3) NOBODY MEASURED THE TWO LARGEST TERMS, AND BOTH TURNED OUT TO BE SURPRISES. The single-sequence-vs-MSA term was treated by Position B as a self-evident excuse and by the proposed experiment as a "cheap rider" expected to be near zero (on the reasoning that plddt 0.9297 and ptm 0.9490 showed the fold was fine). It is +0.811 log10 with SE 0.057, and it points the WRONG WAY: correctly configuring the run makes the prediction worse, moving predicted IC50 from 1.4 µM to 8.9 µM. Structural confidence metrics did not predict the affinity behaviour at all — a warning worth generalising. And the reproducible 0.637-log split between the two affinity checkpoints — visible in the very JSON both sides were quoting from, sign-stable across all nine of my runs — is the largest single contributor to the corrected budget, and neither side mentioned it. The forensic report noticed the split but filed it as "noise"; it is not noise, it is model-form uncertainty, and it means the reported value is the midpoint of two instruments that persistently disagree by more than a factor of four.

(4) THE ERROR THEY FOUGHT OVER WAS THE ARITHMETIC SUM OF TWO LARGE OPPOSITE MISTAKES. The referent-selection bias is −1.265 log10 (the panel drew the joint-most-potent tier out of 23 independent documents, and the four most potent records in the entire set are the four with the worst provenance: three "unknown origin"/unspecified and one that is amyloid-beta aggregation, not catalysis). The configuration-plus-pooling bias is +0.988 log10. They nearly cancel. 2.41 was numerically close to the defensible 2.13 by coincidence. Both disputants were reasoning about a number that had no valid derivation, and the fact that it happened to land near the right answer is the most dangerous possible outcome — it would have validated the wrong method. Related and worth recording: the forensic report's own claim that this pair is "1.4× noisier than the generic ChEMBL IC50 floor" is itself a pooling artifact. Stratify by provenance and the explicitly-human catalytic records give SD 0.539 (n=12) versus 1.336 for the species-unspecified records (n=11), F = 6.14, p = 0.006, with statistically identical means. Provenance controls dispersion, not location. Filtered properly, this compound-target pair is QUIETER than Kalliokoski's generic 0.68 floor, not noisier — which means the reference was never the problem. The referent SELECTION was.

The general lesson for the platform: before any panel argues about a discrepancy, someone has to write down the measurand, run the instrument more than once, and state a coverage factor. Two hours of compute answered a question that two panels of argument could not, and the answer changed both the number and its meaning.

new_positions.discipline: Philosophy of science — evidence and confirmation theory (with statistics)
new_positions.reasoning:
DIAGNOSIS OF POSITION A'S LOGICAL STRUCTURE

A's argument has three links, and they are of three different kinds. Naming them separately is the whole job, because A is valid at link 1, self-refuting at link 2, and fallacious at link 3.

Link 1 — base rate to instance. "AChE is among the most heavily assayed targets in ChEMBL, therefore this pair is more likely memorised than not." This is direct inference (the statistical syllogism): from a known frequency in a reference class to a probability for a member of that class. It is a legitimate defeasible inference, not a fallacy. The classic base-rate-to-instance error is the opposite move — ignoring a base rate — or applying a base rate to an instance for which a narrower, better-supported reference class is available. Here no narrower class was available to A at the time, and the forensic replication has since converted the inference into something close to a lookup: five assays containing Huperzine A x CHEMBL220 pass every reproducible clause of Boltz-2's own published extraction predicate, verdict PROBABLY_IN. So A is NOT committing a base-rate-to-instance error at link 1. A's premise is right, and has been independently corroborated. This should be conceded plainly, because it is the part of A that survives.

Link 2 — the self-refuting step, and the real fallacy. A's inference is: memorised AND wrong by 2.41 log, therefore damning. But the memorisation hypothesis is what fixes which label counts as the target. If the model memorised this pair, what it memorised is the label set the training filter admitted: 21, 33, 47, 47 and 5280 nM, mean pIC50 7.02. It did not memorise 5.0 nM, because all three 5.0 nM records fail Boltz-2's own curation predicate (4, 7 and 4 eligible datapoints against a >=10 threshold), and one of them (CHEMBL1771986) is an amyloid-aggregation readout, not catalytic inhibition. A therefore scored the memorisation hypothesis against a reference that the memorisation hypothesis itself excludes. This is not a base-rate error; it is an internal inconsistency between the hypothesis under test and the operationalisation of its test. Against the label the hypothesis actually predicts, the error is ~1.12 log, and the prediction (pIC50 5.895) falls inside the published human-AChE range for the compound. A's strongest premise destroys A's headline number.

Link 3 — instance to population. "Therefore a strong prior against the affinity head performing on THIS PROJECT'S CHEMISTRY." This is hasty generalisation from n=1, and it is the converse of the error A is accused of: not base rate to instance, but instance to base rate. It is aggravated by the fact that the instance was selected for being the most-assayed possible case — precisely the least representative sample of "this project's chemistry," which by construction includes compounds with thin or no ChEMBL coverage. There is a further conceptual confusion doing real work: a prior is what one holds BEFORE the evidence. Labelling a one-observation posterior a "strong prior" installs it upstream of future evidence, where it will never be updated. That is not a slip of phrasing; it is the mechanism by which an n=1 result becomes unfalsifiable.

DIAGNOSIS OF POSITION B'S LOGICAL STRUCTURE

B advances four grounds and then a conclusion, and B's problem is that the grounds are of unequal strength and B leans on the weakest one.
(i) n=1;
(ii) cherry-picked reference;
(iii) misconfigured run (empty MSA);
(iv) reference metadata unrecorded (standard_type NULL).
Ground (iv) is factually false: all three 5.0 nM records carry standard_type = "IC50", units nM, relation "=", pchembl 8.30. The NULL was an artifact of the project's own retrieval path. B asserted a property of ChEMBL that is a property of the project's code — a striking instance of mistaking an instrument reading for the world. Ground (iii) is asserted, not measured; the single-sequence run still returned ptm 0.949 and complex_plddt 0.930, so the fold was not degraded, and the penalty on this receptor is unknown. Ground (ii) is B's real and decisive point, and B underplays it. Ground (i) is the one B foregrounds, and it is the one that cannot carry the weight.

IS B'S STANDARD SELF-DEFEATING? YES, AS STATED; NO, AS IT SHOULD HAVE BEEN STATED.

Taken literally — "a single non-random observation licenses nothing" — the standard is self-defeating in exactly the way the question anticipates. It would retire every positive single-pair result the project later obtains, and it would also retire large parts of ordinary scientific practice: one counterexample refutes a universal generalisation; one crystal structure settles a fold; one Eddington plate moved belief. Confirmation theory does not license a "licenses nothing" verdict on grounds of count. On any likelihoodist or Bayesian account, an observation E is evidentially inert with respect to H only if P(E|H) = P(E|~H). Sample size does not enter that condition. n=1 sets a bound on PRECISION, not a switch on RELEVANCE. B has confused an estimator's variance with an observation's likelihood ratio.

And the standard is asymmetrically dangerous. Applied consistently it is merely sterile; applied as it usually is — invoked against unwelcome results and forgotten for welcome ones — it is a ratchet. Whatever rule retires the huperzine datum must be written down now and applied to the first single-pair success the platform produces, or the project has adopted a bias, not a standard.

The defensible version of B's position is not about n at all. It is: post-hoc selection of the comparison, not the count of comparisons, is the defeater. A pre-registered single prediction against a pre-specified reference protocol can be strong evidence. A post-hoc single prediction against a post-hoc-selected reference is weak evidence regardless of sign. That reformulation is not self-defeating, it lands B's conclusion, and it survives symmetric application — because it disciplines the project's future successes on exactly the same terms.

WHAT I COMPUTED, AND WHY IT SETTLES THE WEIGHT QUESTION

Neither side ever computed how much the observation should move anyone's belief. I did, from the dossier's retrieved anchors only (Boltz-2 mean blinded MAE 1.217 log10 over 8 private assays; Table 15's 30.7% within 1 log uncentered; the in-situ reference sigma ~0.93-0.99 for this exact pair). Modelling "the head works at its published level" as a folded normal with sigma = 1.217*sqrt(pi/2) = 1.525, and "the head is uninformative on this chemistry" as roughly uniform over the compound's own 3.99-log ChEMBL range (sigma 2.30):

  |e| = 1.12 (the honest error) -> P(|e| >= this | head works as published) = 0.463; LR(broken:works) = 0.77
  |e| = 1.24 -> P = 0.416; LR = 0.80
  |e| = 1.44 -> P = 0.345; LR = 0.85
  |e| = 2.41 (the disputed figure) -> P = 0.114; LR = 1.33

Two things follow. First, at the honest error the likelihood ratio is BELOW one — the observation, correctly referenced, points very slightly TOWARD the head working as advertised, because a ~1.1-log miss is the modal outcome of a head with a 1.217-log published MAE. Second, even at the inflated 2.41 the LR is 1.33: about a fifth of a bit. My Gaussian is conservative in A's favour — it implies P(|e|>1) = 0.512 where the retrieved Table 15 value is 0.693, so the true distribution is heavier-tailed and the real LR is closer still to 1. A single observation on this target would have to miss by ~3.5 log to reach LR = 3 and ~4.7 log to reach LR = 10.

So B's CONCLUSION is approximately correct and now quantified: the datum is worth a fraction of a bit. But B reached it by a rule about sample size that is false, and would have reached the same verdict for a hypothetical 4.7-log miss that genuinely would have been decisive. Right answer, wrong reason, and the wrong reason is the one being written into the project's standards.

VERDICT

A is right on the fact (PROBABLY_IN, corroborated by replication of the published predicate) and wrong on the inference, twice: it scored its own hypothesis against a label that hypothesis excludes, and it generalised from the least representative possible instance while calling the result a prior. B is right on the bottom line and wrong on the stated standard, wrong on the NULL-metadata claim, and unsupported on the MSA claim. Neither is entitled to a settled view of the affinity head. The one experiment that can adjudicate is the stratified rank-recovery design already proposed — and note that it is decisive precisely because the estimand it targets, a DIFFERENCE of two within-arm correlations, is not merely imprecise at n=1 but undefined at n=1. That, not sample size in the abstract, is the exact sense in which the huperzine observation could never have settled this.

SIX THINGS, ORDERED BY WHAT THEY ARE WORTH.

1. NEITHER SIDE EVER NAMED THE ALTERNATIVE HYPOTHESIS, SO NEITHER WAS ARGUING ABOUT EVIDENCE AT ALL. Evidential relevance is a three-place relation: E supports H relative to a rival H' against background K. Both disputants argued a two-place question — is this observation admissible? — which has no answer in confirmation theory. "The affinity head is bad" is not a hypothesis until you say bad COMPARED TO WHAT. Once you supply the rival, the dispute evaporates: against "the head performs at its own published blinded level (MAE 1.217 log10)", the honest 1.12-log error yields LR(broken:works) = 0.77 and the inflated 2.41 yields 1.33. The observation is at or near the MEDIAN of the model's own published error distribution. It was never a test. Everything both sides said about admissibility was downstream of a question neither asked.

2. THE 2.41 IS A STATISTIC OF THE SEARCH PROCEDURE, NOT OF THE MODEL — AND THIS IS ARITHMETICALLY DEMONSTRABLE. The reference was not given; it was FOUND, by scanning 25 records whose own single-measurement sigma is 0.93-0.99 for this exact pair. For n draws at sigma, E[max deviation from centre] ~ sigma*sqrt(2 ln n). At n = 25 and sigma = 0.945 that is 2.40 log10. The disputed discrepancy is 2.41. Across the plausible sigma range (0.93-0.99) and n (23-25) the expectation spans 2.33-2.51 — the observed value sits in the middle. In other words: if the model had predicted the reference set's exact centre, and you then went looking for the record most distant from your prediction, you would expect to find one about 2.4 log away. The disputed number is the expected value of a maximum-selection statistic. A read a property of its own retrieval procedure as a property of the model. B sensed this ("cherry-picked") but never computed it, and so could not distinguish "somewhat selected" from "entirely constituted by selection." This single calculation is the most decisive thing in the file and neither camp produced it.

3. BOTH TREATED THE REFERENCE AS A FIXED POINT WHEN IT IS A RANDOM VARIABLE OF THE SAME ORDER AS THE RESIDUAL. This is a classic errors-in-variables failure. The reference sigma for this pair is ~0.99; the model's own two ensemble members disagreed by 0.729 log on this very prediction (-0.2593 vs +0.4696); the honest residual is ~1.1-1.4. When the denominator's noise and the predictor's internal noise are each of the same magnitude as the thing you are attributing to model error, no attribution is possible — not "is difficult," but is formally not identified. A treated 5.0 nM as truth. B attacked the reference's METADATA rather than its VARIANCE, and got the metadata claim factually wrong. The right objection was never metadata; it was that ChEMBL disagrees with itself about this pair by more than 2.41 log in 8% of its own internal pairwise comparisons.

4. THE MODEL SHIPPED ITS OWN LIKELIHOOD RATIO IN THE OUTPUT FILE AND BOTH IGNORED IT. affinity_probability_binary = 0.4447 — the model declined to assert that the ligand binds. iptm = 0.7136, below the 0.75 threshold Boltz-2's own authors used to ADMIT assays into the affinity training corpus, i.e. this complex as predicted falls beneath the quality bar of the training distribution by the authors' published criterion. And the ensemble spread was 0.729 log. The model announced, three independent ways, that this prediction was outside its competence. Using a self-flagged low-confidence prediction as a test of a model is selection on the PREDICTOR side, exactly mirroring the selection on the reference side — the datum was chosen twice for extremity, once at each end. In evidential terms, conditioning on a low-confidence flag drives P(large error | H_works) upward, which drives the LR toward 1 and beyond. Both sides argued about a number while the uncertainty shipped alongside it went unread. That is the single most damning oversight in the record.

5. DISCOVERY VERSUS JUSTIFICATION — B'S REMEDY IS AIMED AT THE WRONG TARGET. B wants the datum "retired as motivation." Motivations do not require evidential warrant; hunches, anomalies and aesthetic dissatisfactions are legitimate and unregulated inputs to the context of discovery. What requires warrant is the context of justification. So B's prescription is backwards: the project should KEEP the huperzine anomaly as motivation — it is cheap, directionally suggestive, and it generated a genuinely good experimental design — and stop quoting 2.41 as a FINDING. Conflating the two contexts is how projects end up either paralysed (no hunch may be acted on) or credulous (every hunch is a result). The concrete rule: the number may appear in a Motivation section and nowhere else, and it may never appear with a decimal point attached to a claim about model quality.

6. ENDPOINT POOLING IS A STRUCTURAL BIAS TERM THAT NEITHER SIDE PRICED. Boltz-2 maps Ki, Kd, IC50, XC50, EC50 and AC50 onto one log10(uM) target with NO inter-endpoint offset, while Kalliokoski shows pKi and pIC50 require ~0.35 log of offset to be comparable, and the Boltz-2 authors themselves restricted their own affinity VALIDATION set to Ki only "to ensure a higher degree of experimental consistency." So a portion of any absolute error measured against an IC50 reference is a known, signed, structural artifact of the training target definition — not model incompetence in the sense A means, and not noise in the sense B means. It is a third category both sides lack a slot for. Its magnitude is unquantifiable because the paper reports no endpoint proportions, which is itself the finding: absolute-error claims against this head carry an irreducible unknown bias, and that is a permanent argument for ranking metrics over absolute ones — independent of everything else in this dispute.

CLOSING OBSERVATION FROM MY DISCIPLINE. The deepest structural point is that both camps were trying to extract a CONTRAST from a POINT. The quantity that would settle "is it recall or skill" is a difference between two conditional performances, stratified on training-set membership. A difference is not merely imprecisely estimated by one observation — it is undefined for one observation, because one observation occupies one stratum. That is why the panel deadlocked, and why no amount of further care about huperzine A could have broken it. B was reaching for this and grabbed the wrong instrument (sample size) instead of the right one (the estimand is a contrast). Say it that way and B's position stops being self-defeating, A's position stops being answerable by assertion, and the proposed stratified study becomes the obvious and only next move.

resolution:
# ADJUDICATION — Boltz-2 affinity head, Huperzine A × human AChE

**Chair's note on scope.** The previous panel's ruling was procedural. This one is not. I have re-verified the load-bearing numbers against the artefacts on this machine rather than inheriting them, and where the three new disciplines disagreed with each other I have ruled rather than averaged. Two of the four factual questions that were open at the start of this session are now closed by measurement, not by argument.

---

## 1. THE RULING

**Position A loses the dispute. Position B wins the disposition, and every argument B gave for it is struck.**

That is not a split. A and B were arguing about *what the observation licenses about this project's chemistry*. On that question A is wrong, and A is wrong for reasons that its own strongest premise generates. B reached the correct disposition, but not one of B's four stated grounds survives contact with the evidence, and the standard B proposed ("a single non-random observation licenses nothing") is a rule the project must not adopt.

### What is now settled, and on what evidence

**(a) The 2.41 figure is a statistic of the retrieval procedure, not of the model. Decisive, and arithmetic.** The reference was not given; it was found, by scanning 23 IC50 records for this pair whose own dispersion is SD 0.980 log, and selecting the joint-3rd-most-potent tier. I simulated the selection directly (200,000 replicates, N(µ = 1.201, σ = 0.980), n = 23 draws, actual predicted pIC50 5.895):

| order statistic of the discrepancy | E[value] | SD |
|---|---|---|
| largest | 3.09 | 0.50 |
| 2nd largest | 2.65 | 0.38 |
| **3rd largest** | **2.39** | **0.33** |
| random record | 1.20 | 0.98 |

P(3rd largest ≥ 2.406) = **0.467**. The observed 2.406 sits at the median of what the selection procedure produces. Decomposition: **2.41 = 1.20 (the model's real offset against the pooled reference mean) + 1.19 (pure selection) + 0.02 (residual).** Half the disputed quantity is the retrieval path. A read a property of its own search as a property of the model; B sensed this and never computed it, and so could not distinguish "somewhat selected" from "half constituted by selection."

**(b) B's misconfiguration plank is refuted with the sign reversed. Measured, and I re-verified it from the raw JSON.** Nine runs of the identical input exist in this session's artefacts:

- single-sequence, n = 6 (incl. the disputed run): y = 0.1052, 0.1924, 0.1194, 0.0250, 0.1798, 0.2055 → **mean 0.1379, SD 0.0685**
- real ColabFold MSA (depth ~11k), n = 3: y = 1.0216, 0.9696, 0.8543 → **mean 0.9485, SD 0.0856**
- **configuration effect = +0.811 log10, SE 0.057 (t ≈ 14)**

Running it the way the vendor intends moves predicted IC50 from 1.4 µM to **8.9 µM** — 0.81 log *further* from every candidate reference. The "misconfigured run" excuse is not unproven; it is false, and inverted. It may not be raised again for this receptor.

**(c) The instrument's repeatability is excellent and was never the problem.** `--seed` defaults to `None`; every number in this dispute came from one unseeded draw. Six replicates give SD 0.068 log. The panel was accidentally safe on precision and unsafe on everything else.

**(d) The forensic ipTM finding is void.** "This run sits below the 0.75 training-admission bar (ipTM 0.7136)" is an artifact of one unseeded draw. Across the six single-sequence replicates ipTM ran 0.714–0.841, **four of six above 0.75**; and one MSA run returned 0.550, so MSA does not reliably raise it either. Struck. By contrast `affinity_probability_binary` is genuinely stable (0.422–0.463 SS; 0.344–0.380 MSA) — the low binder probability is real.

**(e) B's NULL-metadata claim is false, and the error is this project's.** All three 5.0 nM records carry `standard_type = "IC50"`, units nM, relation "=", pchembl 8.30. The project's own ledger already contains the correction (`clm_cfc50f17bdec6f4b`): the code read the key `type` where the field is `activity_type`, and the actually-null field is `assay_confidence`. B asserted a property of ChEMBL that is a property of our retrieval code.

**(f) A's premise is right and A's inference is self-refuting.** Training-set membership is PROBABLY_IN — five assays clear every reproducible clause of Boltz-2's published extraction predicate. But the memorization hypothesis is what fixes the target label, and the labels it admits are 21, 33, 47, 47, 5280 nM (mean pIC50 **7.02**). All three 5.0 nM records *fail* that predicate (4, 7, 4 eligible datapoints against a ≥10 threshold); one, CHEMBL1771986, is an amyloid-β-aggregation readout — a peripheral-anionic-site phenotype, not catalytic inhibition. **A scored the memorization hypothesis against a reference the memorization hypothesis excludes.** Independently, the provenance-clean stratum (12 records whose assay description names the enzyme source) gives mean pIC50 **7.036 ± 0.156**. Two entirely different routes converge to within 0.02 log. That is the reference.

**(g) The "noisy pair" premise is an annotation artifact, and it inverts.** Stratified by whether the assay names its enzyme source: source-stated n = 12, SD **0.539**; unspecified n = 11, SD **1.336**; means statistically identical (Δ = 0.13, t = 0.29); variances not (F = 6.14, p = 0.006). Provenance controls dispersion, not location. Filtered properly this pair is **quieter** than Kalliokoski's generic σ_pIC50 = 0.68, not 1.4× noisier. The whole 3.99-log range lives in the unannotated half — and the four most potent records in the set are the four with the worst provenance. The reference population was never the problem. The referent *selection* was.

**(h) A's inference is a category error about direction of inference.** A's conclusion is a population claim ("this project's chemistry"). The standard uncertainty of a mean error estimated from one compound is σ_between-compound ≈ 1.53 log, so the generalization estimate is **2.16 ± 3.06 (k = 2) = [−0.90, +5.22]** — it contains zero. A computed a pair-level uncertainty (±0.74) and used it to license a population-level claim carrying ±3.06. Aggravated by the fact that the instance was selected for being the *most*-assayed possible case, i.e. the least representative sample of a project whose chemistry is largely novel.

**(i) A's "strong prior" is a one-observation posterior wearing a prior's clothes.** Labelling it a prior installs it upstream of future evidence, where it will never be updated. That is the mechanism by which n = 1 becomes unfalsifiable, and it is why this must be refused explicitly rather than merely discounted.

### Where B is wrong even though B wins

B's stated standard — "a single non-random observation licenses nothing" — is false and, worse, is a ratchet. Evidential relevance is not a function of sample size: E is inert with respect to H only when P(E|H) = P(E|¬H), and n does not enter that condition. n = 1 bounds *precision*, not *relevance*. Applied consistently the rule retires every future single-pair success the platform obtains; applied as such rules usually are — against unwelcome results, forgotten for welcome ones — it is a bias with a methodological costume.

**The correct rule, which the project adopts: post-hoc selection of the comparison, not the count of comparisons, is the defeater.** A pre-registered single prediction against a pre-specified reference protocol can be strong evidence. A post-hoc single prediction against a post-hoc-selected reference is weak regardless of sign. That reformulation lands B's conclusion, is not self-defeating, and binds the project's future successes on identical terms.

And B's "it licenses nothing" is too strong. Something real survives (§3).

### What remains undecidable, and whether it is obtainable here

**Undecidable now: whether the affinity head's skill on AChE is memorization-dependent.** Not because the huperzine observation is imprecise, but because the estimand is a *contrast* — a difference between two conditional performances stratified on training-set membership — and a contrast is **undefined** at n = 1, since one observation occupies one stratum. No amount of further care about huperzine A could ever have broken this deadlock. That is the exact sense in which both camps were arguing past the question.

**Obtainable here: yes.** The stratified rank-recovery design in §4, on this MacBook, in two 10-hour nights, using ChEMBL v34-vs-v37 bulk dumps to convert membership from a prior into a lookup. No cluster, no cloud.

**Not obtainable here, and stop claiming otherwise:** confirmation of membership. The affinity split is unreleased, no processing script ships in the repo, and the assay-level ipTM ≥ 0.75 gate is not reproducible. `PROBABLY_IN` is the ceiling from outside. Anyone asserting CONFIRMED_IN or CONFIRMED_OUT is overclaiming; one email to Boltz/MIT would close it and is worth sending.

**Closed as a non-issue:** the receptor. Both the disputed run (`/private/tmp/aff/in.yaml`) and the study construct (`/tmp/ache_mature.txt`) contain the identical 583-residue P22303 mature chain, SHA-256 `b5db97836a739e0eee92ef5e185431d900a1a16f9170041d2d5a55aba8b80475`. The "543-residue" figure recurs ~20 times in `reviews/idea_panel.json` and is simply wrong. The two camps were not arguing about different receptors.

---

## 2. THE UNCERTAINTY BUDGET

**Measurand.** D = pIC50(reference) − pIC50(prediction), log10 units, where predicted pIC50 = 6 − `affinity_pred_value`. Note at the outset that the instrument and the reference measure different quantities: the head's target is a pooled log10(µM) potency over Ki/Kd/IC50/XC50/EC50/AC50 with **no inter-endpoint offset**, while the reference is a pure IC50. That is a traceability failure, not a performance finding, and it is why an absolute-error claim against this head carries an irreducible unknown bias.

### Budget A — the 2.41 figure exactly as the panel constructed it

| term | source | u (log10) | % variance |
|---|---|---|---|
| u₁ run-to-run repeatability | Type A, n = 6, SD 0.0685 | 0.068 | 0.4% |
| u₂ ensemble model-form split | half of mean \|y₁−y₂\| = 0.637 | 0.319 | 7.8% |
| u₃ endpoint pooling, no offset | rectangular on [0, 0.355], 0.355/√12 | 0.102 | 0.8% |
| u₄ single ChEMBL record as referent | SD of the 23-record population | 0.980 | 74.1% |
| u₅ configuration left undecided | rectangular on the 0.811 effect, /√3 | 0.468 | 16.9% |

u_c = √(0.068² + 0.319² + 0.102² + 0.980² + 0.468²)
= √(0.004624 + 0.101761 + 0.010404 + 0.960400 + 0.219024) = √1.296213 = **1.139**

U(k = 2) = **2.28**.  **D = 2.41 ± 2.28 (95%)**, z = 2.11, lower bound **+0.13**.

**Is 2.41 distinguishable from zero? Two answers, and the distinction is the whole ruling.**

*As a raw difference:* barely — by 0.13 log, one coverage factor's worth of honesty from evaporating. The dispute was fought over a quantity whose expanded uncertainty is 95% of its own value.

*As evidence of anomalous model error: no, and not marginally.* Budget A's u₄ models the referent as a **random draw**. It was not: it was the 3rd-most-extreme of 23. Under the correct sampling model the selection procedure alone contributes **+1.19 log**, and the observed 2.406 sits at the **47th percentile** of what that procedure produces (E = 2.391, SD 0.333). There is no excess over the selection expectation to attribute to the model. **2.41 is not distinguishable from zero excess error.** It is the expected output of the search.

### Budget B — bias-corrected, the estimate that should have been reported

Corrections applied to D: referent selection (5.0 nM cherry → provenance-clean 7.036) **−1.265**; endpoint pooling **+0.177**; configuration, if moving to vendor-intended MSA mode **+0.811**.

| predicted pIC50 | 5.862 | 5.052 |
| reference pIC50 | 7.036 ± 0.156 | 7.036 ± 0.156 |
| raw D | 1.174 | 1.985 |

| **D_corr** | **1.351** | **2.162** |

u_c (MSA) = √(0.049² + 0.319² + 0.102² + 0.156²) = √0.138900 = 0.373 → U(k=2) = **0.75**

1. measured pIC50, 0.5-log bins, 1:1 greedy nearest-neighbour (kills range restriction, the precondition for comparing two correlations at all);

The provenance clause is not fastidiousness. ### Primary metric

**Δρ_S = ρ_S(S1) − ρ_S(S3)**, the difference in within-target Spearman rank correlation between predicted and curated measured pIC50, computed separately in each potency-matched arm. One-sided α = 0.05. **Governing inference: 10,000-permutation within-bin label shuffle.** BCa bootstrap CI over compounds (10,000 resamples; resampling over compounds, never over individual measurements). If permutation and Fisher-z disagree, permutation governs — fixed in advance.

Why rank, not absolute error: it is the axis the objective optimises (Huber loss on absolute values and, *with stronger weight*, on pairwise intra-assay differences, introduced expressly because "this difference-based formulation implicitly cancels out assay-specific confounding factors"); it is offset-invariant and the offset is enormous (Table 15: 1.7001 uncentered vs 0.8569 centered — 0.843 of pure per-assay constant); it survives the reference noise floor, which absolute error does not; it is robust to the 7-log outliers this corpus contains (huprine X 0.026 nM, pralidoxime 340,000 nM); and — decisively — **it is a per-arm quantity, so it can be differenced across strata.** A pooled metric cannot express a memorization gradient at all, which is the entire dispute. Absolute error is the *first secondary*, never the headline. Early enrichment is deferred and named here so nobody proposes it later: at n = 75 per arm EF@1% is decided by a single molecule.
